source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN Examination, 7th ed.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which symptom does the nurse expect in newly diagnosed Hodgkin's disease?
questions.rationale: Hodgkin's typically presents with night sweats, painless enlarged nodes, fever, and malaise.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q33 (PDF p. 172)
questions.quote: Assessment of a client with Hodgkin’s disease most often reveals night sweats; enlarged, painless lymph nodes

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which finding suggests acute rejection after a kidney transplant?
questions.rationale: Acute rejection, usually within 3 months, causes fever, hypertension, malaise, graft tenderness, and less urine.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q49 (PDF p. 189)
questions.quote: Acute rejection usually occurs within the first 3 months after transplant

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which home measure helps oral mucositis from head and neck radiation?
questions.rationale: Mucositis care includes gentle oral hygiene and frequent mild rinses such as saline; alcohol and irritants are avoided.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q53 (PDF p. 193)
questions.quote: Oral mucositis (irritation, inflammation, and/or ulceration of the mucosa) also known as stomatitis

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: By the rule of nines, burns to both entire legs and the perineum are about what percent?
questions.rationale: Each leg is 18% (36%) plus the perineum 1% = 37%.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q81 (PDF p. 226)
questions.quote: The most rapid method used to calculate the size of a burn injury in adult clients

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Which finding supports mittelschmerz?
questions.rationale: Mittelschmerz is pelvic pain midway between periods at ovulation.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q87 (PDF p. 233)
questions.quote: Mittelschmerz (middle pain) refers to pelvic pain that occurs midway between menstrual periods

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Which statement shows understanding of endometriosis?
questions.rationale: Endometriosis is tissue resembling endometrium outside the uterus that responds to hormones during the cycle.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q88 (PDF p. 234)
questions.quote: Endometriosis is defined as the presence of tissue outside the uterus that resembles the endometrium

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which plan prevents skin breakdown in a client with a pelvic fracture?
questions.rationale: Pressure injury prevention includes minimizing force and friction, regular repositioning, and keeping skin clean and dry.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q93 (PDF p. 241)
questions.quote: Interventions for prevention of pressure injuries include minimizing the force and friction applied to the skin

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which finding is MOST indicative of stage II Lyme disease?
questions.rationale: Stage II (1–3 months) includes dysrhythmias, dyspnea, dizziness, and neurologic problems. Arthritis marks stage III.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q104 (PDF p. 253)
questions.quote: The most serious problems in this stage include cardiac dysrhythmias, dyspnea, dizziness

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which finding is expected in stage III Lyme disease?
questions.rationale: Stage III features arthritic symptoms such as arthralgia and enlarged, inflamed joints.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1109 (PDF p. 1393)
questions.quote: It is characterized by arthritic symptoms such as arthralgia and enlarged or inflamed joints

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which sign is characteristic of pemphigus vulgaris?
questions.rationale: Nikolsky's sign, where the epidermis rubs off with slight friction, is a hallmark, with flaccid bullae.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q105 (PDF p. 254)
questions.quote: A hallmark sign of pemphigus vulgaris is Nikolsky’s sign

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: An anxious client with a finger laceration has pulse 106 and BP 158/88. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: Stress triggers sympathetic stimulation causing tachycardia and high BP; stress reduction helps.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q133 (PDF p. 283)
questions.quote: Physical or emotional stress triggers sympathetic nervous system stimulation.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which skin care shows understanding during radiation therapy?
options: Protect from heat, cold, and sun
questions.rationale: Treated skin is protected from temperature extremes, sun, and chlorinated water; markings are kept.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q189 (PDF p. 342)
questions.quote: The client undergoing radiation therapy must keep the affected skin protected from temperature extremes, direct sunlight, and chlorinated water

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: After right radical mastectomy, which intervention is included?
options: Blood draws from the right arm
Check the back of the dressing
questions.rationale: Drainage seeps down by gravity to the posterior axillary dressing first, so it is checked. No BP or draws on the affected arm.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q198 (PDF p. 352)
questions.quote: gravity will cause the drainage to seep down and soak the posterior axillary portion of the dressing first.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Where does a burn heterograft come from?
questions.rationale: Heterograft is skin from another species, most often pig. Homograft is human (cadaver); autograft is the client's own.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q216 (PDF p. 371)
questions.quote: Heterograft is skin from another species.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which describes early Kaposi's sarcoma lesions?
questions.rationale: Kaposi's sarcoma starts flat and pink and turns dark violet or black, usually bilaterally.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q226 (PDF p. 381)
questions.quote: Kaposi’s sarcoma generally starts with an area that is flat and pink that changes to a dark violet or black color.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which discharge instruction fits a client after testicular cancer surgery?
questions.rationale: The client reports chills, fever, drainage, redness, or discharge to the provider.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q297 (PDF p. 460)
questions.quote: the nurse should emphasize the importance of notifying the primary health care provider if chills, fever, drainage, redness

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which plan ensures safe cancer pain control?
questions.rationale: Safe pain control starts with low doses and titrates up to relief, alongside nondrug measures.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q468 (PDF p. 652)
questions.quote: Safe pain control includes starting with low doses and working up to a dose of medication that relieves the pain.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Which problem should adoptive parents be counseled about?
options: No need to tell the child
questions.rationale: Adoptive parents may set unrealistically high standards and may lack the child's biological history.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q615 (PDF p. 828)
questions.quote: Adoptive parents may add pressure to themselves by setting unrealistically high standards

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client with AIDS is losing weight. What should the nurse advise?
questions.rationale: Nutrient-dense, high-calorie food in small, frequent meals supports weight gain.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q617 (PDF p. 831)
questions.quote: The client who has a problem with nutrition and is losing weight should take in nutrient-dense and high-calorie meals

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Which statement after vasectomy needs MORE teaching?
questions.rationale: Birth control continues until semen analysis shows no sperm; live sperm may remain in the vas.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q626 (PDF p. 843)
questions.quote: the client must continue to practice a method of birth control until the follow-up semen analysis shows azoospermia.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which statement about prostate cancer is correct?
questions.rationale: Smoking and a history of STIs raise risk; yearly digital rectal exams aid early detection.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q627 (PDF p. 844)
questions.quote: Smoking, history of a sexually transmitted infection, and yearly digital examinations are accurate statements

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Which husband's statement on preventing infertility needs MORE teaching?
questions.rationale: Keeping the testes cool by avoiding hot baths and tight clothing appears to improve sperm count.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q628 (PDF p. 845)
questions.quote: Keeping the testes cool by avoiding hot baths and tight clothing appears to improve the sperm count.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: After lung cancer surgery, which statement needs MORE teaching?
options: 'I'll handle more pain on my own.'
questions.rationale: Increasing pain should be reported; clients are not expected to manage it alone.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q658 (PDF p. 877)
questions.quote: The client who just had surgery for lung cancer should not be expected to deal with increases in pain independently.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: How can a client with AIDS reduce recurrent thrush?
questions.rationale: Careful routine mouth care helps prevent overgrowth of Candida in immunosuppression.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q750 (PDF p. 979)
questions.quote: an overgrowth of the normal flora Candida can occur.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which food should a client with AIDS avoid?
questions.rationale: Avoid raw or undercooked seafood, meat, poultry, eggs, and unpasteurized dairy.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q751 (PDF p. 980)
questions.quote: The client who is at risk for immunosuppression is taught to avoid raw or undercooked seafood, meat, poultry, and eggs.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which sign suggests an opportunistic respiratory infection in AIDS?
questions.rationale: Fever and exertional dyspnea are signs of Pneumocystis jiroveci pneumonia.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1094 (PDF p. 1377)
questions.quote: Fever and exertional dyspnea are signs of Pneumocystis jiroveci pneumonia

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which is an appropriate goal for a client with AIDS at risk for PCP?
questions.rationale: PCP causes fever, exertional dyspnea, and nonproductive cough; a goal is effective breathing without dyspnea.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1306 (PDF p. 1607)
questions.quote: A common, life-threatening opportunistic infection that occurs in clients with AIDS is Pneumocystis jiroveci pneumonia.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A family wants hospice for a client with terminal throat cancer. What is a main goal of hospice?
questions.rationale: Hospice emphasizes caring rather than curing, with the client free of pain and distressing symptoms.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q842 (PDF p. 1079)
questions.quote: Hospice care provides an environment that emphasizes caring rather than curing

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: How is acute cancer pain BEST assessed?
questions.rationale: The client's perception, usually rated 0–10, is the hallmark of pain assessment.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q843 (PDF p. 1080)
questions.quote: The client’s perception of pain is the hallmark of pain assessment.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client with AIDS feels socially isolated. What is MOST useful?
questions.rationale: The nurse encourages social contact and reduces barriers, including educating family about transmission.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q988 (PDF p. 1238)
questions.quote: The nurse encourages the client to maintain social contact and support

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client's first HIV ELISA is positive and she cries. What should the nurse know?
options: The test is repeated and confirmed
questions.rationale: A positive ELISA is repeated because of possible false positives and confirmed with Western blot.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q994 (PDF p. 1244)
questions.quote: If the client tests positive for HIV with the ELISA test, the test is repeated because of the potential for a false-positive result

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Before cystectomy, which statement shows FEAR?
questions.rationale: Fear has an identifiable object; here the uncertain outcome of surgery.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q996 (PDF p. 1247)
questions.quote: For fear to be an actual problem, the client must be able to identify the object of fear.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client says, 'My cancer spread; I have less than 6 months.' What is MOST therapeutic?
questions.rationale: The client is likely in shock and denial; inviting ventilation of feelings is therapeutic.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1008 (PDF p. 1259)
questions.quote: In option 1, the nurse invites the client to ventilate feelings.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which statement during external radiation needs MORE teaching?
questions.rationale: Lotions and powders are not applied without specific provider instructions.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1077 (PDF p. 1359)
questions.quote: The client receiving external radiation therapy should avoid pressure on the irritated area and wear loose-fitting clothing.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which statement shows a client with AIDS learned energy conservation?
questions.rationale: Sitting for activities such as dressing, shaving, cooking, and bathing conserves energy.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1079 (PDF p. 1361)
questions.quote: The client is taught to conserve energy by sitting for as many activities as possible

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which statement about thrush care needs MORE teaching?
questions.rationale: Commercial mouthwashes with alcohol cause pain; warm water or saline rinses are used.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1081 (PDF p. 1363)
questions.quote: Clients with thrush cannot tolerate commercial mouthwashes because the high alcohol concentration

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which finding fits moist desquamation from radiation?
questions.rationale: Moist desquamation destroys basal cells and exposes the dermis, which leaks serum.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1105 (PDF p. 1389)
questions.quote: Moist desquamation occurs when the basal cells of the skin are destroyed.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: How is a client positioned for intraperitoneal chemotherapy?
questions.rationale: IP chemotherapy is infused into the peritoneal cavity with the client in semi-Fowler's for comfort and breathing.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1173 (PDF p. 1462)
questions.quote: IP therapy is the administration of chemotherapeutic agents into the peritoneal cavity.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: What should a client with very dry, irritated skin apply?
questions.rationale: Emollients treat dry, cracked, irritated skin. Muscle rubs are for aches; acetic acid is for wound irrigation.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1179 (PDF p. 1469)
questions.quote: A topical emollient is used for dry, cracked, and irritated skin.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Which statement shows understanding of laser surgery for cervical cancer?
questions.rationale: Laser therapy is outpatient, painless, and used when lesion borders are visible; no general anesthesia.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1349 (PDF p. 1652)
questions.quote: Laser therapy is performed in an outpatient setting and is used when all boundaries of the lesion are visible.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: When do fibrocystic breast symptoms usually worsen?
questions.rationale: Lumps and tenderness worsen before menses because of hormonal changes.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1370 (PDF p. 1673)
questions.quote: The client with fibrocystic breast disorder experiences worsening of symptoms

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: After radical vulvectomy, which discharge plan shows best understanding?
questions.rationale: Activity resumes slowly; walking helps, with rest when fatigued. Driving and heavy work are avoided.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1372 (PDF p. 1675)
questions.quote: The client should resume activity slowly, and walking is a beneficial activity.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Before bilateral orchiectomy, a 25-year-old needs priority exploration of which concern?
questions.rationale: Loss of reproductive ability is a major psychological concern and is a priority to address.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1376 (PDF p. 1679)
questions.quote: the nurse should place priority on addressing loss of reproductive ability

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A man treated for syphilis before has a new penile lesion. Which feature suggests reinfection?
questions.rationale: The syphilis chancre is painless and indurated. Warts are cauliflower-like; herpes causes painful vesicles.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1378 (PDF p. 1681)
questions.quote: The characteristic lesion of syphilis is painless and indurated.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which finding is expected in infiltrating ductal breast carcinoma?
questions.rationale: It usually presents as a single, unilateral, fixed, irregular, hard, painless mass.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1391 (PDF p. 1694)
questions.quote: Infiltrating ductal carcinoma of the breast usually presents as a fixed, irregularly shaped mass.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: After mastectomy with node dissection, which plan shows correct arm care?
options: Carry heavy bags on that arm
Have BP taken on that arm
questions.rationale: The client avoids trauma to the affected arm (gloves for gardening) to prevent edema and infection.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1394 (PDF p. 1698)
questions.quote: The client is at risk for edema and infection as a result of lymph node dissection.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A COPD client on 2 L O2 has RR 22 and reports dyspnea. What should the nurse do FIRST?
questions.rationale: Further assessment comes first; oxygen is not raised without validation because of CO2 retention risk.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1413 (PDF p. 1719)
questions.quote: Completing an assessment and collecting additional information regarding the client’s respiratory status is the initial nursing action.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which finding is expected in systemic lupus erythematosus?
questions.rationale: SLE may cause fever, aches, a butterfly facial rash, pleural effusion, lymphadenopathy, and pericarditis.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1439 (PDF p. 1747)
questions.quote: Manifestations of SLE may include fever, musculoskeletal aches and pains, butterfly rash on the face

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client on chemo has a falling WBC. Which precaution is MOST appropriate?
questions.rationale: Low WBC means infection risk. Padding rails and removing sharps are bleeding precautions.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1443 (PDF p. 1752)
questions.quote: Padding the side rails and removing all hazardous and sharp objects from the environment would be instituted if the client is at risk for bleeding.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: After cervical cryosurgery, what discharge is expected?
questions.rationale: Discharge is clear and watery after cryosurgery; pain is mild.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1455 (PDF p. 1764)
questions.quote: Vaginal discharge should be clear and watery after the procedure.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which behavior shows the MOST difficulty adjusting after mastectomy?
options: Refuses to look at the dressing
questions.rationale: Refusing to look shows she is not ready to acknowledge the loss.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1492 (PDF p. 1801)
questions.quote: The client demonstrates the most difficult adjustment to the loss if she refuses to look at the dressing.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which exercise is done in the first 24 hours after mastectomy?
questions.rationale: In the first 24 hours, the client moves fingers and hands and flexes and extends the elbow.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1502 (PDF p. 1811)
questions.quote: During the first 24 hours after surgery, the client is assisted to move the fingers and hands, and to flex and extend the elbow.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client on chemo has platelets of 15,000/mm³. Which precautions apply?
questions.rationale: Platelets below 20,000/mm³ place the client at risk for bleeding.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1542 (PDF p. 1854)
questions.quote: When the platelet count is less than 20,000 mm3 (20 × 109/L), the client is at risk for bleeding
